_comment_url: One URL per TEMPLATE, not per page. Three of these were added when the site grew
past the original three: a collection-driven hub, an expert profile and a
hand-built support page were all shipping unmeasured. Adding a page to an existing
template does not need a new entry here; adding a new template does.
hub -> owner-builder-courses (HubLayout via a stub route)
cpd -> cpd (hand-built, converts to a hub in B3; drop this then)
styleguide -> the component gallery, heaviest page in the build

_comment_styleguide: The component gallery, held to its own LCP budget. It renders all 34 components
on one page, is noindex and excluded from the sitemap, and is never served to a
reader: it is the heaviest page in the build BY DESIGN and representative of no
real page. At 1800ms it sat exactly on the CI runner's boundary and flipped at
random - measured 1804, 1805, 1806 and 1807 on failing runs and under 1800 on
passing ones, with no code change between them. Locally the same build measures
1506-1512ms across five runs, so the runner is ~300ms slower than a dev machine.
A gate that fails a coin flip blocks merges without ever catching a defect.
2200ms keeps it a real check (a genuine regression here would be far larger than
400ms) while leaving the five production URLs strict at 1800. Every other
assertion below is unchanged, including minScore 1.
_comment_tbt: MOVED HERE 13 Aug 2026, from inside the `assertions` object below. lhci reads every key
of `assertions` as an audit id, so this comment was being asserted as one, and printed
on every run:
✘  _comment_tbt failure for auditRan assertion
"_comment_tbt" is not a known audit.
It did not fail the build, which made it worse rather than better: it was the ONLY line
the assertion step emitted (there is no 'all passed' message), so the gate's entire
visible output was a failure that was always false, and a real one would have arrived
as a second ✘ in a place readers had been trained to ignore. This sibling position is
where `_comment_url` and `_comment_styleguide` already sit, and neither has ever been
parsed as an audit. Keep comments OUT of `assertions`; anywhere else in the file is fine.
total-blocking-time raised from 50 to 100 for THIS PAGE ONLY, 1 Aug 2026, for exactly
the reason the LCP budget above was raised: it flaps on the runner. Measured on two CI
runs of BYTE-IDENTICAL page output, PR #106 and PR #105, where the only difference
between the branches was two markdown files that render nothing: 24ms on one run, and
58ms on the other (individual runs 58, 59, 55). A 2.4x swing with no code change is not
a signal, and this exact page has done this before at 1800ms LCP.
The five production URLs stay at 50 and are untouched. This page renders all 34
components at once, is noindex, is excluded from the sitemap and is never served to a
reader, so it is the one page where a heavier main-thread cost is expected and means
nothing about what a visitor gets. 100ms still leaves it a real check: Lighthouse treats
TBT under 200ms as good, the highest value ever observed here is 59, and a genuine
regression on a page this heavy would be far larger than 40ms.
Do NOT copy this number to a production URL. If a production page ever needs it, that
is a defect to fix, not a budget to raise.
